record.original_question: If a compact surface in Euclidean 3-space E^3 is of finite type, meaning that its position vector is a finite sum of Laplacian eigenmaps, must that surface be a sphere?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. The only compact finite type surfaces in E^3 are the spheres.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subset \mathbb{E}^3$ be a compact (closed, without boundary) smooth surface isometrically immersed in Euclidean 3-space, with position vector $\mathbf{x} : M \to \mathbb{E}^3$ and Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ acting componentwise on $\mathbf{x}$. The surface $M$ is said to be of finite type if its position vector admits a decomposition
$$\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x}_0 + \mathbf{x}_{1} + \mathbf{x}_{2} + \cdots + \mathbf{x}_{k},$$
where $\mathbf{x}_0 \in \mathbb{E}^3$ is a constant vector and $\mathbf{x}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{x}_k$ are non-constant $\mathbb{E}^3$-valued maps on $M$ satisfying $\Delta \mathbf{x}_i = \lambda_i \mathbf{x}_i$ for pairwise distinct real numbers $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_k$.

Prove or disprove: every compact finite-type surface in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is a round sphere.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, due to B.-Y. Chen (1980s), asserts that round spheres are the only compact finite-type surfaces in E^3. Recent literature (e.g. works on surfaces of finite Chen-type from 2015 onward) continues to refer to it as an open problem; partial results exist for special classes (ruled, quadric, tubes, surfaces with finite-type Gauss map), but no full resolution has been reported.

status_evidence.title: On Surfaces of finite Chen-type (Stamatakis, Al-Zoubi)
status_evidence.snippet: Up to this moment the only known finite Chen-type surfaces in E^3 are portions of spheres, circular cylinders and minimal surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open; only partial classifications known.

status_evidence.title: On Surfaces of Finite Type in Euclidean 3-Space (Kodai Math. J.)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies finite-type surfaces in E^3, addressing Chen's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Problem framed as Chen's conjecture; partial results obtained.
